content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices, especially in bullish sentiment periods.", "Sentiment spikes often precede sharp price corrections, indicating model overconfidence.", "Model forecasts show minimal mean-reversion, failing to capture sudden volatility in true outcomes.", "High sentiment positivity correlates with forecast overshoots, suggesting sentiment drives model bias.", "True outcomes frequently dip below forecasts during early 30-day windows, indicating lagged reaction to sentiment.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment is neutral or negative, suggesting sentiment moderates model drift.", "Models exhibit persistent upward bias in early forecast periods, even when true prices show downward momentum.", "Sentiment history should be weighted more heavily in model calibration to reduce forecast overshoots."]}
